solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Polenta for dinner?

parts.note: polenta is boiled maize flour, i.e. ground corn that has been prepared on the stove, served as the evening course

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether polenta would do for the evening meal.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'dinner' as the hot food on the plate, and polenta as ground maize that has been boiled.
explanation.definitionFit: Polenta is literally ground maize that has been heated in water, and a dinner is a prepared evening repast.

clue.text: Deal with hoodie

definitions.meaning: to manage or handle a situation successfully
a long ecclesiastical cloak, traditionally with a hood, worn by clergy in processions

explanation.surface: An instruction to handle a hooded youth.
explanation.definitionFit: To deal with a problem is to manage it; the clerical vestment of that name once had a hood attached.

clue.text: Attack one left lashing out indiscriminately

indicators.note: done without order or selection, so the remaining letters are thrown into a new arrangement
here meaning departed, so the letter for one goes out of the phrase

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: An assault by one person, left-handed perhaps, flailing wildly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one left' means I has gone from LASHING OUT, leaving LASHNGOUT; 'indiscriminately' shuffles those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A fierce, overwhelming assault is an onslaught, so the noun sense of attack matches.

clue.text: Stand before court

parts.note: ere is the poetic word for before

explanation.surface: An instruction to stand up in front of a law court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stand' is the verb, as in standing a ladder up.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand something upright, such as a pole or a statue, is to put it up vertically.

clue.text: Princess bride without social graces

indicators.note: in its old sense of outside, so the bride's title wraps round the princess

parts.note: a bride takes the title Mrs, abbreviated MRS
Princess Anne, the Princess Royal

explanation.surface: A royal bride who lacks any sense of etiquette.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like lacking, but means outside here.
explanation.definitionFit: Good etiquette and polite behaviour in company are collectively called one's manners.

clue.text: Commercial peak for consultant

parts.note: an advertisement on TV is a commercial, abbreviated AD
the peak of a cap, shading the eyes, is its visor

explanation.surface: A consultant hired to help a business reach peak commercial performance.
explanation.definitionFit: A consultant is someone paid to give expert counsel, which is exactly the role of an adviser.

clue.text: Burden of our financial responsibility

definitions.meaning: a duty or responsibility that weighs on someone
split as two words, the bill is '...' when we are paying

explanation.surface: A statement that paying is down to us.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is the answer split in two: when we pay, it is on us.
explanation.definitionFit: A burden is an obligation or duty, and the Latin-derived word for that duty is used in English for responsibility.

clue.text: Welshman and Scotsman sharing singular setback with beautiful spirit

indicators.note: set back is read as turned backwards, so the joined names run in reverse
the two names share one letter rather than each having its own, so one copy goes

parts.note: Dai is a stock Welsh first name
Ian is a stock Scottish first name
I is the singular first-person pronoun, and the letter both names hold

explanation.surface: A Welshman and a Scot jointly suffer a single reverse involving a lovely ghost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sharing singular' means the two names use one I between them rather than one each; 'setback' turns the joined result round.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth a water nymph of springs and rivers is a naiad, a lovely nature spirit.

clue.text: Topiarian trees sited in tranquil spot

indicators.note: topiary clips hedges into new shapes, so these letters are reshaped too

explanation.surface: Clipped shrubs planted in a peaceful garden corner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topiarian' is the anagram signal: TREES SITED is reshaped.
explanation.definitionFit: A minor road off the main thoroughfare is typically quiet, so it is a fair, loose description of a tranquil spot.

clue.text: Old hat is father's sombrero — origin Spain

parts.note: pa is father, so father's gives PA'S

indicators.note: the origin of a word is its first letter

parts.note: E is the international vehicle registration for Spain

explanation.surface: Dad's Mexican hat is out of date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old hat' is the definition, not a garment: the sombrero is only fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Something old hat is out of fashion, the meaning of the French borrowing for outmoded.

clue.text: Driven men prepared not to worry

indicators.note: something prepared has been made ready or arranged, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Determined men were ready, so there was no cause for concern.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase used to tell someone to forget a matter is an idiom for 'don't worry about it'.

clue.text: Slimmer and longer-legged from artificial rearing

indicators.note: artificial means made up rather than natural, so the letters are made into a new word

explanation.surface: Animals bred artificially turn out leaner and leggier.
explanation.definitionFit: A rangy person or animal is long-limbed and slender; the comparative form means more so.

clue.text: Simple — unlike Charles Saatchi

definitions.meaning: Saatchi is a famous British collector of contemporary art, so someone with no art is unlike him

explanation.surface: A jibe that an art collector is anything but straightforward.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles Saatchi is a British advertising man famous for his huge contemporary art collection.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone simple and unaffected is guileless, which is the ordinary meaning; read whimsically it means having no paintings.

clue.text: Paintings produced regularly from mid-1700s

indicators.note: produced at regular intervals, so every other letter is taken

parts.note: 1700s spelt out is seventeen hundreds; its middle-to-end stretch, starting at the last N of seventeen, is the run used

explanation.surface: Pictures turned out steadily since about 1750.
explanation.walkthrough: Spell out 1700s as SEVENTEEN HUNDREDS; from its middle, at NHUNDREDS, take alternate letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Paintings of unclothed human figures are a classic genre in art, each such picture being a nude.

clue.text: Enter Gaga with tailored rump pants — that's an entrance!

indicators.note: British slang pants means rubbish or a mess, so these letters are made a mess of
the rump is the hind end, so the last letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: Lady Gaga arrives in fitted trousers, making quite an entrance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tailored rump' is the D ending tailored; 'pants' (British slang for rubbish) shuffles ENTER GAGA plus D.
explanation.definitionFit: A gate set in a hedge or wall to let you into a garden is a literal way in, an entrance.

clue.text: White City is large redevelopment

indicators.note: redevelopment rebuilds an area in a new layout, so the letters are rebuilt

explanation.surface: A west London district called White City is being heavily rebuilt.
explanation.walkthrough: White City is a district of London, but here it is the nickname of the Algerian capital, known as 'la Blanche' for its whitewashed buildings.
explanation.definitionFit: The North African capital is nicknamed the white one in French for its gleaming whitewashed houses.

clue.text: Beatle got ripped to bits for pretentious solo project

indicators.note: only a bit of the phrase is used, so the answer lies inside the words

explanation.surface: A Beatle got torn apart for a self-indulgent solo album.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ripped to bits' suggests an anagram, but the letters sit unbroken across BeatlE GOT RIPped.
explanation.definitionFit: A venture undertaken mainly to flatter oneself is a vanity exercise, like a self-indulgent solo record.

clue.text: Discount the odds of bacillaceae being found in Rolls-Royce heads' vehicle

indicators.note: one string is located inside the other, so it is placed within the outer letters
the heads of the two names are their first letters
ignore the odd-numbered letters and keep only the even ones

explanation.surface: Bacteria are found in the heads of Rolls-Royce owners' cars.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters of BACILLACEAE give AILCA, which goes between the two Rs that head Rolls and Royce.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-propelled passenger coach running on rails is a type of vehicle.

clue.text: Clean home gets makeover with one matching wallpaper?

indicators.note: a makeover redoes something in new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A spruced-up home includes a feature that matches the decor.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is playful: a lizard that changes colour could blend into the wallpaper.
explanation.definitionFit: The lizard famous for changing its skin colour to match its surroundings could blend into wall decor.

clue.text: Motown trio broke up in debt with departure of Jackson brothers' nucleus

indicators.note: the shuffled trio is placed inside what remains of debt
the following letter leaves the word debt
the nucleus is the central letter of the two-word phrase
a group that broke up has split, so the letters are scattered

explanation.surface: A Motown trio split up in debt after the Jacksons' core left.
explanation.walkthrough: The central letter of JACKSON BROTHERS is B; removing it from DEBT leaves DET, which holds TROI, an anagram of TRIO.
explanation.definitionFit: Motown is a contraction of Motor Town, the nickname of the Michigan car-making city.

clue.text: Nominal thank you — cloaking it with outwardly ungrateful resistance

indicators.note: a cloak covers, so the thanks wrap around the next letters

parts.note: ta is informal British for thank you

indicators.note: the outside letters of the word are taken

parts.note: R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A token thanks wrapped in grudging resistance.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is informal British for thank you; 'cloaking' wraps it round both 'it' and the outside of 'ungrateful'.
explanation.definitionFit: A titular head holds the title in name only, so the word means nominal.

clue.text: Vanishing era for wine levy?

definitions.meaning: split in two, a period of stoppers made from bark, now disappearing as screw caps take over
a charge a restaurant makes for opening a bottle the diner brings

explanation.surface: A wine tax may be on its way out.
explanation.walkthrough: Screw caps are replacing natural bark stoppers, so the age of those stoppers is passing.
explanation.definitionFit: A restaurant's fee for serving wine the customer has brought is a charge or levy on that bottle.

clue.text: Detailed conversation on pointless notices all over the place

indicators.note: in a down answer, one piece sits on top of the other
de-tailed, so the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a chat is a conversation

indicators.note: without compass points, so the letters for north, east and south go

parts.note: taken as written before the cut

explanation.surface: A long talk about pointless notices that are scattered everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Detailed' means tail removed, not thorough. Compass points N, E and S leave NOTICES as OTIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Something all over the place is disordered and in confusion, which is the sense of the answer.

clue.text: Drain off the pits

indicators.note: off means gone bad or out of order, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Draining something from the pits of a mine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the pits' looks like literal holes, but it is slang for the worst point.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang 'the pits' means the absolute worst, and the lowest point of anything is its nadir.

clue.text: Similarly over-the-top personality trait in the ascendant

indicators.note: rising, so in a down answer the letters read upwards

parts.note: OTT is the usual abbreviation for over the top
in Freud the id is the instinctive part of the personality

explanation.surface: An exaggerated character trait that is on the rise.
explanation.walkthrough: OTT plus ID gives OTTID; 'in the ascendant' turns it upwards in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The word used to say 'the same again' or 'likewise' is an adverb meaning in the same way.

clue.text: Stir pea soup for slattern

indicators.note: something in the soup is mixed up, so the letters are stirred together

explanation.surface: A cook stirring pea soup for a slovenly woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soup' is the anagram signal, and 'Stir' is fodder, not an instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: As a dated noun, the word names a slovenly, untidy woman, which is what a slattern is.

clue.text: Outstanding US author — not 60 — dead

indicators.note: not means without, so the following numeral is removed

parts.note: Annie Proulx is the American author of The Shipping News
LX is sixty in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A distinguished American novelist who died short of sixty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outstanding' means sticking out, as a proud nail does.
explanation.definitionFit: Something standing out from a surface, as a nail head does, is proud of it.

clue.text: Unsatisfactory 1 across

indicators.note: the number points to the 1 across entry, whose first word, a kitchen term for prepared, serves as the signal to rearrange

parts.note: with the number, names the 1 across entry, whose second word, ground grain, is the fodder

explanation.walkthrough: The 1 across solution, read as wordplay, is an anagram signal ('cooked') followed by its fodder ('meal').
explanation.definitionFit: Lame is informal for weak or unconvincing, as with a feeble excuse.

clue.text: George's pilau too spicy — bin half of it

indicators.note: a spicy dish is hot and lively, so these letters are stirred up
throw away one of its two letters

parts.note: taken as written before the cut

explanation.surface: George finds his rice dish too hot and throws half away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'George' is RAF slang for the device that flies a plane; the 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Airmen nicknamed the automatic flight-control system George, as if a crewman were flying.

clue.text: Closure of 'Chicago' the prelude to quiet time for musical drama

indicators.note: a prelude comes before, so this letter precedes the next
the closing letter of the word

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: The end of the show 'Chicago' leads into quiet time before a stage piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chicago' is a musical, but here it gives only its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A sung stage drama with orchestra is the classic form of musical theatre.

clue.text: A glimpse of Alderney — otherworldly island

indicators.note: a glimpse sees only part, so the answer is a portion of the words

explanation.surface: A brief sight of the Channel island of Alderney, which looks unearthly.
explanation.walkthrough: Alderney is itself an island, a tempting definition; the answer is in aldernEY OTherworldly.
explanation.definitionFit: A small river islet, especially on the Thames, is called an eyot (also ait).

clue.text: Priority change limiting decline — almost

indicators.note: limiting means bounding on both sides, so one goes round the other

parts.note: small coins are change, here pence

indicators.note: almost means the final letter is lost

parts.note: to decline or ebb away is to recede

explanation.surface: Coping with change while curbing a near decline comes first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' here is loose coins, not alteration; 'limiting' means enclosing, and 'almost' drops the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Precedence is the right to come first, the same as priority in order or importance.
